'''vulvate''' (vul′vāt), ''a.'' [< ''vulva'' + ''-ate''<sup>1</sup>.] Shaped like or formed into a vulva; vulvar; vulviform.

'''vulviform''' (vul′vi-fôrm), ''a.'' [< L. ''vulva'', womb, + ''forma'', form: see ''form''.] '''1.''' In ''zoöl.'', shaped like the vulva of the human female; oval, with raised lips and a median cleft.—'''2.''' In ''bot.'', like a cleft with projecting edges.

'''vulvismus''' (vul-vis′mus), ''n.'' [NL., < L. ''vulva'', vulva.] Same as ''vaginismus''.

'''vulvitis''' (vul-vī′tis), ''n.'' [NL., < L. ''vulva'' + ''-itis''.] Inflammation of the vulva.

'''vulvo-uterine''' (vul-vō-ū′te̤-rin), ''a.'' Of or pertaining to the vulva and the uterus: as, the ''vulvo-uterine'' canal (the vagina).

'''vulvovaginal''' (vul-vō-vaj′i-nal), ''a.'' Pertaining to the vulva and the vagina.—'''Vulvovaginal canal.''' {{smaller|Same as ''vagina''.}}—'''Vulvovaginal glands,''' {{smaller|the glands of Bartholin or odoriferous glands in the female, corresponding to Cowper’s glands in the male. See ''gland''.}}

'''vulvovaginitis''' (vul-vō-vaj-i-nī′tis), ''n.'' [NL., < ''vulva'' + ''vagina'' + ''-itis''.] Inflammation of both the vulva and the vagina.

'''vum''' (vum), ''v. i.'' A corruption or equivalent of ''vow'', used in the expression “I ''vum'',” a mild expletive or oath. Compare ''swan''<sup>2</sup>. [New Eng.]
{{smaller block|<poem>The Deacon swore (as Deacons do,
With an “I dew ''vum'',” or an “I tell yeou”).</poem>
{{right|''O. W. Holmes'', Deacon’s Masterpiece.}}}}

'''vummera,''' ''n.'' Same as ''wummerah''.

'''V-vat''' (vē′vat), ''n.'' In ''mining'', a pointed or V-shaped box in which crushed or pulverized ores are sized or classified by the aid of water. {{smaller|The earthy particles mingled with the ore entering above fall against a current of water rising from beneath, the velocity of which is regulated so that a more or less complete separation of the ore from the gangue is effected. These boxes are generally arranged in a series of four or more, and there are many varieties of the apparatus, of which the general principle was the invention of Von Rittinger, an Austrian metallurgist. This method has proved to be of great value in ore-dressing. Also called ''pointed box'', ''pyramidal box'', and ''spitzkasten''.}}

<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="transcriber" />{{RunningHeader|vulturine|6796|vysar}}</noinclude>the cere and toes are yellow, the eyes are umber-brown, and the beak is horn-color.—'''Vulturine guinea-fowl''', the naked-necked guinea-fowl, ''Acryllium vulturinum''. This is a remarkable form, with the head and upper part of the neck nearly bare, like a vulture’s, the lower neck, the
breast, and fore back plumaged with very long discrete lance-linear feathers of black, white, and blue color; the narrow acuminate middle tail-feathers long-exserted; the general plumage black, spotted with white; the lower {{smaller|breast light-blue; and the flanks purple, ocellated with black and white. This guinea-fowl inhabits Madagascar as well as various parts of continental Africa.—'''Vulturine raven,''' the vulture-raven.—'''Vulturine sea-eagle,''' an occasional erroneous name of the Angola vulture of West Africa. See cut under ''Gypohierax.''}}

[[File:century v08 p0600 c1f1.png|center|91px]]

'''vulturish''' (vul′tṳ̄r-ish), ''a.''   [< ''vulture'' + ''-ish''<sup>1</sup>.]   Same as ''vulturine'', 2.
{{smaller block|Hawkish, aquiline, not to say ''vulturish.''
{{right|''Carlyle'', Misc., IV. 245. (''Davies.'')}}}}

'''vulturism''' (vul′ṭūr-izm), ''n.''   [< ''vulture'' + ''-ism.'']   Vulturine character or quality; rapacity.   ''Carlyle.''

'''vulturn''' (vul′tėrn), ''n.''   [Arbitrary var. of ''vulture'', appar. through ''vulturine.'']   The brush-turkey of Australia, ''Talegallus lathami'': so named from the nakedness of the head suggesting a vulture. See cut under ''Talegallus.''

'''vulturous''' (vul′ṭūr-us), ''a.''   [< ''vulture'' + ''-ous.'']   Like or characteristic of a vulture.
{{smaller block|Such gawks (Gecken) are they, and foolish peacocks, and yet with such a ''vulturous'' hunger for self-indulgence.
{{right|''Carlyle'', Sartor Resartus, ii. 4.}}}}

'''vulva''' (vul′vạ̈), ''n.''   [= F. ''vulve'' = Sp. Pg. ''vulva'' = It. ''volva'', < L. ''vulva'', ''volva'', a covering, integument, womb, < ''volvere'', roll around or about: see ''volve'', ''volute.'']   '''1.''' In ''anat.'', the external organs of generation of the female; especially, the orifice of these parts, the external termination of the vagina—of an elliptical contour in the human female.—'''2.''' In ''entom.'', the orifice of the oviduct.—'''3.''' In ''conch.'', the oval or vulviform conformation presented by certain bivalve shells when the right and left valves are in apposition. See ''Veneridæ.''—'''Velamen vulvæ.''' {{smaller|See ''velamen.''}}—'''Vestibule of the vulva.''' {{smaller|See ''vestibule.''}}

'''vulvar''' (vul′vär), ''a.''   [< ''vulva'' + ''-ar''<sup>3</sup>.]   Of or pertaining to the vulva; vulviform.—'''Vulvar canal.''' {{smaller|Same as ''vulva'', 2.}}—'''Vulvar enterocele.''' {{smaller|(''a'') A vaginal hernia protruding through the vulva. (''b'') A hernia which has descended between the ramus of the ischium and the vagina into one of the labia majora; pudendal enterocele or hernia.}}—'''Vulvar hernia.''' {{smaller|Same as ''vulvar enterocele.''}}

'''vulvate''' (vul′vāt), ''a.''   [< ''vulva'' + ''-ate''<sup>1</sup>.]   Shaped like or formed into a vulva; vulvar; vulviform.

'''vulviform''' (vul′vi-fôrm), ''a.''   [< L. ''vulva'', womb, + ''forma'', form: see ''form''.]   '''1.''' In ''zoöl.'', shaped like the vulva of the human female; oval, with raised lips and a median cleft.—'''2.''' In ''bot.'', like a cleft with projecting edges.

'''vulvismus''' (vul-vis′mus), ''n.''   [NL., < L. ''vulva'', vulva.]   Same as ''vaginismus''.

'''vulvitis''' (vul-vī′tis), ''n.''   [NL., < L. ''vulva'' + ''-itis''.]   Inflammation of the vulva.

'''vulvo-uterine''' (vul-vō-ū′te̤-rin), ''a.'' Of or pertaining to the vulva and the uterus: as, the ''vulvo-uterine'' canal (the vagina).

'''vulvovaginal''' (vul-vō-vaj′i-nal), ''a.'' Pertaining to the vulva and the vagina.—'''Vulvovaginal canal.''' {{smaller|Same as ''vagina''.}}—'''Vulvovaginal glands,''' {{smaller|the glands of Bartholin or odoriferous glands in the female, corresponding to Cowper’s glands in the male. See ''gland''.}}

'''vulvovaginitis''' (vul-vō-vaj-i-nī′tis), ''n.''   [NL., < ''vulva'' + ''vagina'' + ''-itis''.]   Inflammation of both the vulva and the vagina.
